title: AuthorizeRequest v1
description:
Body of POST /v1/authorize. The full, explicit input vector for a deterministic authorization decision.

Determinism contract (ROADMAP A#7): the decision is a pure function of (this request, the active policy_version, evaluated_at, counter_snapshot). Predicates MUST NEVER read the wall clock, RNG, or the network themselves — every time-dependent or stateful input is injected here by the orchestrator (evaluated_at, counter_snapshot). This is what makes decisions replayable.

Auth note: request authentication (API key + HMAC signature + nonce + timestamp) travels in HTTP HEADERS, not in this body — it is a separate, symmetric concern from the Ed25519 signature on the Decision. See the OpenAPI security scheme.

agent_id.description: Identifier of the autonomous agent initiating the transaction (the subject whose delegated authority is being checked).

action.description: The action the agent wants to take, dotted namespace. Matched by agent_permission predicates.

amount.description: Transaction amount as a canonical decimal string, in `currency`. String (not number) for exact money precision and stable signing canonicalization.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction the transaction is evaluated under. Optional but recommended; jurisdiction_currency predicates require it.

context.description: Arbitrary caller-supplied key/value context (e.g. invoice_id). Available to predicates as read-only data. Kept free-form on purpose; keep it small and non-sensitive where possible.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-generated key that makes authorize retry-safe: an identical request replayed with the same key returns the SAME decision and does not create a second budget hold (TRD §9). Use a UUID or ULID.

evaluated_at.description: ORCHESTRATOR-INJECTED. The single instant the decision is evaluated against; time_window and any time-dependent predicate read THIS, never the wall clock. Clients SHOULD NOT set it — the authorize service stamps it on intake and echoes it on the Decision. Present in the schema because it is part of the frozen, replayable input vector (ROADMAP A#7).

counter_snapshot.description: ORCHESTRATOR-INJECTED. Point-in-time accumulator readings (budgets/velocity) the stateful predicates consume. Clients SHOULD NOT set it — the orchestrator resolves counters and injects them so budget decisions are deterministic and replayable (ROADMAP A#3, A#7). Absent when no stateful predicate applies.
